rejected.title: Wave and particle models of light
card: A model is a way of explaining how something behaves. Scientists use two models for light, because one model cannot explain everything light does.
Wave model
light travels as a wave. It explains why light spreads out after passing through a narrow gap and why it bends when it moves from air into water.
Particle model
light is a stream of tiny packets of energy called photons. It explains why light is absorbed in separate amounts of energy, such as when a solar cell takes in light.
Neither model is wrong. Each one explains some behaviour of light, so scientists choose the model that fits what they are studying.
rejected.remember: Spreading and bending fit the wave model. Absorption fits the particle model.

a.q: Light from a torch passes through a narrow slit and spreads out on the other side. Which model best explains this?
opts: The wave model, because waves spread after a gap
The particle model, because photons spread after a gap
The wave model, because waves are absorbed in packets
The particle model, because photons bend in water
a.why: Spreading out after a narrow gap is a wave behaviour, so the wave model explains it. The particle model is tempting, but it is used for absorption, not for spreading.
a.clue: Think about which behaviour belongs to which model.

b.q: Priya's solar cell takes in light and gives out electricity. Which model best explains how the cell takes in the light, and why?
opts: Particle model, as photons are absorbed as packets of energy
Wave model, as waves are absorbed as packets of energy
Particle model, as photons spread out after a narrow gap
Wave model, as light bends when it enters the glass cover
b.why: Absorption is explained by the particle model, where each photon hands over a packet of energy. The wave model does not explain absorption. Bending in the glass cover is a real wave behaviour, but it is not how the cell takes in light.
b.clue: The question is about absorbing light, not bending it.
